correctness.rationale: Condition on no direct edge; the iid background produces binomial joint probability b(d)^(n-2) and marginals a^(n-2), and strict monotonicity of positive powers yields the sign. Strict radial convolution monotonicity follows via layer-cake intersections of centered circular arcs and positive-measure strict levels; symmetry/Fubini ensures exactly one sign zero. Poisson thinning, exact arc intersections and a one-variable optimizer complete the proof. A packaged standard-library checker passed 8,732 assertions; finite tests do not replace infinite proof.

value.rationale: Poissonization can reverse conditional pair-isolation dependence. A universal single-crossing classification under nontrivial radial kernels, a hard-radius phase cutoff at one-quarter circumference, and a unique sharp maximum 3-2sqrt2 for the prevalence of positive conditioned covariance give a natural complete spatial-statistical invariant that informs finite-population versus Poisson modeling.
